phase_classification_method: BIC-segmentation with k in {1,2,3} constant-mean regimes; nimmaturi2025predictive three-phase criterion = (best_k == 3) AND monotone_up AND (seg1_mean < 0.15) AND (seg3_mean > 0.40) (arXiv:2507.18014).
nemotron_violation: Nemotron-120B is the only 5-anchor pool member classified as 'collapse'. BIC picks k=3 (best segmentation), the segment means are 0.0000;0.8750;0.1544 (rise-then-fall, peak=0.875, late=0.154), and the peak segment mean exceeds the late segment mean. This is a textbook collapse and DIRECTLY violates the nimmaturi2025predictive three-phase template, which requires monotone non-decreasing segment means with seg1_mean < 0.15 and seg3_mean > 0.40 (arXiv:2507.18014).
t80_scaling_law: OLS log10(t_80) ~ log10(N) over 5 anchors: intercept=-0.8413, slope=0.1699, se=0.2538. 4/5 anchors hit the lambda upper bound (t_80 = -ln(0.2)/10.0 = 0.161) and only 1/5 (Nemotron-120B) has a meaningful lambda. The cross-scale t_80 scaling-law test is DEGENERATE: a 5-row column of repeated values prevents any informative slope estimate. LOO and bootstrap CI both confirm the degeneracy.
frontier_synthesis: iter117 Pillar 1 closes the scaling-law investigation by adding (i) explicit t_80 = -ln(0.2)/lambda derivation in the canonical fits table; (ii) BIC-segmentation three-phase test against arXiv:2507.18014 (0/5 anchors pass); (iii) Nemotron-120B collapse audit (peak segment mean = 0.875, late segment mean = 0.154 -- rise-then-fall); and (iv) t_80-vs-N scaling-law test, which is demonstrably degenerate because 4/5 anchors are already saturated at step 1 (lambda at upper bound). Combined with iter109's lambda-vs-N null (p=0.74) and iter105's R_max*(N) failure, the Pillar-1 finding is that GRPO post-training on this evidence base is NOT scale-law-shaped -- the only strong signal is the absence of a scaling law.
